title: RAG Data-Leakage and Access-Control Testing
summary: Test whether your RAG pipeline leaks documents across users, roles or tenants through retrieval, caching, citations or logs, using seeded canary documents and role-based test personas.

seo.title: RAG Data-Leakage and Access-Control Testing | VipraTech
seo.description: RAG security testing: tenant isolation, document permissions, revoked access, cache and log leakage, and indirect prompt injection via uploads.

designed_for: AI Search or Copilot Product Lead

problem.intro: RAG lets your assistant answer from customers' own documents, tickets and records. It also creates a new path to that data: a query, an embedding search and a prompt. If permissions are not enforced at retrieval time, or if caches and logs mix tenants, one customer's question can surface another customer's content.

pain_points.title: Filters applied after retrieval
pain_points.detail: Permissions checked only after the top results are fetched, or only in the UI, can still leak content into the prompt and the answer.

pain_points.title: Shared indexes across tenants
pain_points.detail: A single vector index with metadata filters is only as safe as every query path that remembers to apply them.

pain_points.title: Stale permissions
pain_points.detail: When a user loses access to a document, its chunks often stay retrievable until the next full re-index.

pain_points.title: Leakage outside the answer
pain_points.detail: Citations, semantic caches, analytics events and tracing tools can carry another tenant's chunks even when the answer looks clean.

solution.overview: We test your RAG feature for data leakage and access-control gaps from the outside in and the inside out. We seed each test tenant, role and user with unique canary documents, then use test personas to query through every entry point: chat, search, API and integrations. Any canary that appears in an answer, citation, cache hit, log or trace where it should not is a finding. We also review the retrieval code path, index design and permission sync, test what happens when access is revoked or a document is deleted, and check whether uploaded documents can carry instructions that change the assistant's behaviour. Findings map to OWASP LLM risks for sensitive information disclosure and vector and embedding weaknesses.
capabilities: Canary documents seeded per tenant, role and user to detect leakage
Persona-based queries across chat, search, API and integration entry points
Permission revocation and deletion tests for stale chunks
Cache, citation, analytics and trace leakage checks
Indirect prompt injection tests through uploaded or synced documents
Review of retrieval code paths, index design and permission sync

workflow.title: Map the data path
workflow.detail: We map ingestion, chunking, indexes, permission sync, retrieval, caching and logging for the RAG feature.

workflow.title: Seed canaries
workflow.detail: Unique canary documents are added for each test tenant, role and user.

workflow.title: Query as each persona
workflow.detail: Test personas query through every entry point and try to reach content they should not see.

workflow.title: Change permissions
workflow.detail: We revoke access, delete documents and move users between groups, then query again.

workflow.title: Detect and review
workflow.detail: Canary hits in answers, citations, caches and traces are flagged and confirmed by a tester.

workflow.title: Report and retest
workflow.detail: Findings come with fixes to retrieval filters, index design or sync, and are retested after changes.

inputs: Staging environment with at least two test tenants
Test users for each role and permission level
Architecture of ingestion, vector store and retrieval
Read access to logs, traces and caches in staging
List of connected sources such as Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence or Jira
outputs: Data path diagram with trust boundaries
Leakage findings with exact path and evidence
Fixes for retrieval filters, index design and permission sync
human_in_the_loop: A tester confirms every canary hit and traces the leakage path before reporting it. Your engineers decide on the fix, such as per-tenant indexes or retrieval-time permission checks.
integrations: Vector stores such as pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Elasticsearch or OpenSearch
Connected sources such as SharePoint, Google Drive, Confluence or Jira
Tracing tools such as Langfuse or LangSmith
guardrails: Synthetic canary content only, never real customer documents
Testing limited to test tenants in staging
Findings shared only with named contacts
Read-only access to logs and traces
compliance_notes: Maps to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications categories for sensitive information disclosure and vector and embedding weaknesses.
Evidence of tenant isolation supports obligations on access to personal data under GDPR and the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: One RAG feature with two or three test tenants and its main connected source, tested in staging.

what_we_measure.how: Confirmed canary exposures by path: answer, citation, cache, log or trace.
Time between revoking access and the document no longer being retrievable, measured in tests.
Entry points tested against those in scope.
Leakage paths confirmed closed after fixes.

faqs.q: Do you need access to our customers' data?
faqs.a: No. We work only with synthetic canary documents in test tenants. That is enough to show whether isolation holds.

faqs.q: We use metadata filters in a shared index. Is that unsafe?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. It depends on whether every query path applies the filter and whether caches and logs respect it. Testing shows where the gaps are; some teams then move high-risk tenants to separate namespaces or indexes.

faqs.q: Can uploaded documents change how the assistant behaves?
faqs.a: They can, if retrieved text is treated as instructions. We test this with planted content and recommend ways to keep retrieved data separate from instructions.

faqs.q: How do we keep this tested after the first round?
faqs.a: The canary suite can run in CI on every change to retrieval, indexing or permission sync, so regressions are caught before release.
